task-8.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "Side rail and other UI improvements are important purely because the current ones are just mostly the original ones and are due a bit of a sprinkling. But! The front end code is messy." And his gut: "the UI issues trace back to one of my very first rules: no build step… it's the biggest target of the Theseus method… We don't need to tidy it all, but it's a perfect example where we can leave it better than we found it. Likely this will take a fair amount of hand holding."

On main (9 Nov), no browser file can import another, nine browser files restate logic the server already has, and the largest browser file is 5,019 lines.

On the views, John: "Lots of light little views is ideal, but the cost of them has to be balanced… I'd be sad to get rid, but happy to tidy."

**What we want.**

* Browser code that shares rather than restates. There's still no build step and no framework: the rule stays, read as allowing the browser to import, as browsers do natively, and that reading goes into the project's own notes.
* Taken in small slices, one view or one shared piece at a time. Each view is reworked only after finding out why it got so large, and comes out lighter.
* Anything bigger that a slice spots is left out of it and goes into the area's note.
* The side rail and the visual refresh come after, built on the cleaner code.
* No view is retired unless John rules it.

John expects agents to reach for big moves here: "very likely to get agents trying really hard to do big things when we want small." So the size is John's call, and for this work it's small.

**Done when** the reading of the rule is in the project's notes; the first slice has landed, sharing rather than restating, lighter than before and naming what it retired; and John has read the first slice's result before the next starts.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

fields.says: Survey LIN-4446 @ 4b5001ddf, hard 1: "allow the browser to import" does not turn imports on. `server.js:1228` serves only `public/`, so the server modules a browser file restates (`lib/cost-format.js` etc.) have no URL. Sharing needs a served place for pure modules that both `lib/` and the browser import, plus a rule for it (no Node built-ins, no DOM at load); without the rule someone will import a module that pulls in `node:fs`. CSP `script-src 'self'` already allows module scripts loaded from a file.

Survey LIN-4446 @ 4b5001ddf, hard 2: every page is classic scripts talking through globals. `lib/components/page.js` writes ordered `<script src>` tags; files read `window.X` and top-level bindings from `public/common.js` (3,309 lines, on 29 pages). A classic script can't use static `import`; making a view `type="module"` makes it deferred, strict and module-scoped, so its globals vanish for later scripts. "One view at a time" is blocked until what views read from `common.js` is reachable another way. Keep this out of the first slice; it goes into the area note (`docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`).

Survey LIN-4446 @ 4b5001ddf, hard 3: the test harness assumes classic scripts. 130 unit test files load `public/*.js` through `vm` (`tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js`, plus `runInNewContext` in the parity tests); none use `vm.SourceTextModule`. A browser file that gains an `import` line breaks all of them. That cost is not in the ticket.

Survey LIN-4446 @ 4b5001ddf, hard 4: "lighter" is easy to fake. About 1,985 of `public/observation.js`'s 5,019 lines are comments (ticket history, retuning stories), and 1,456 of `public/common.js`'s 3,309. Cutting comments passes a line count without sharing anything. The why-so-large check (68 commits on `observation.js`) should count logic and commentary separately, and "lighter" be judged on logic.

Survey LIN-4446 @ 4b5001ddf, hard 5: the ticket is a symptom and the repo already says so. `docs/papers/harbour/the-second-copy.md` §9–10 traces the copies to the no-build-step rule read as "no sharing": parity tests and helpers nobody was required to adopt kept the copies alive, and only deleting the old copy ever finished a consolidation. ## Implementation Plan

**Plan status.** Re-grounded at HEAD `4b5001ddf`: `git log --since=2026-11-13T12:08:10Z` over every path named below is empty, so the two surveys (open-0, global) still describe the code. Area notes read: `docs/areas/README.md`, `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md` (its Lessons are 815 bytes of a 6144 cap; its Waiting entries are context, and the ones this slice touches are named in step 6).

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The ask: browser code that shares rather than restates, no build step, taken in small slices, the reading of the rule written into the project's notes, then a pause for John. John ruled the size: just the task, one cost formatter shared, no cuts (the size record above). Done is the ticket's own Done-when, restated as checks:

1. The reading of "no build step" (the browser may import natively, with its limits) is in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`.
2. `lib/cost-format.js` is the only implementation of `formatUsd`: the browser runs those same bytes. `public/cost-format.js` and `tests/unit/cost-format-parity.test.js` are gone, and the PR names them as retired.
3. The PR says, in numbers, what got lighter (restated logic: the 34-line IIFE gone, replaced by a shim of a few lines) and does not count comments as lightening. It also says plainly that total repo lines may not fall, because the new guards are tests.
4. The builder then **stops**. No second slice starts before John has read the result.

Cuts to the `## As asked` block: **none**. Reworking a view "after finding out why it got so large" is not delivered here; that is John's size ruling (this slice touches no view), not a cut by this plan, and it goes to the area note as Waiting.

### Which way, and why

* **Serve the shared module through the existing allow-list in** `lib/vendor-assets.js`, as a second frozen map (`SHARED_MODULES`: URL → repo file; first entry `/shared/cost-format.js` → `lib/cost-format.js`), validated with `statSync` at boot like `VENDOR_ASSETS`. Set aside: a second `express.static('lib')` (would publish all server source); moving the file into `public/` (server `lib/render-*.js` would import from the web root, and the file would no longer sit with the code that owns it). `VENDOR_ASSETS` stays untouched because `tests/unit/vendor-assets.test.js` pins exactly its three URLs; sharing one router factory is fine, sharing one map is not.
* **Bridge to the classic scripts with a deferred module shim**, `public/cost-format-global.js`: imports `formatUsd` from `/shared/cost-format.js` and sets `window.CostFormat = { formatUsd }`. No view becomes a module, `common.js` and the `vm` loaders are untouched. Set aside: converting a consumer to a module (needs a module-capable client test loader, its own slice, per surveys); keeping `public/cost-format.js` as a thin wrapper (keeps a file whose name claims to be the formatter).
* `lib/components/page.js` **learns one thing: a** `scripts` **entry may be** `{ module: '/x.js' }`, emitted as `<script type="module" src>`; plain strings stay classic. Explicit beats sniffing a filename. The shim goes where `/cost-format.js` was in each list, so the read order of the lists is kept (a module still runs deferred wherever it sits).
* **Retirement is integral:** the restated formatter and its parity test go in the same PR as the sharing (the failed-consolidation pattern in `docs/papers/harbour/the-second-copy.md` §9–10).
* Fits the constraints already ruled: leaf modules only (no imports, no Node built-ins, no DOM at load); no wholesale `lib/` exposure.

### Where the behaviour lives (every place, in scope)

"The browser has its own formatUsd" lives in these places. How I know I have them all: `grep -rIn "cost-format\|CostFormat" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` outside `docs/reviews|papers|plans` (dated records, left as written) — repeat it after building; it must return only the intended new names.

* **Renderers listing** `/cost-format.js` **— five, not the two the brief names:** `lib/render-flight-companion.js`, `lib/render-observation.js`, `lib/render-swipe.js`, `lib/render-task-page.js`, `lib/render-workspace-kpis.js`. (The brief missed swipe, task-page and workspace-kpis; swipe and task-page load `prompt-section.js`, which reads `window.CostFormat`.) Left unfixed, those pages would 404 the script and throw `TypeError` on the first cost.
* **Consumers (read** `window.CostFormat` **— all four read it inside functions today):** `public/flight-companion.js:428`, `public/observation.js:3992`, `public/prompt-section.js:1506`, `public/workspace-kpis.js:134,138`. No change to them.
* **Golden:** `tests/fixtures/render-task-page-golden.json` embeds the script tags: regenerate it by the repo's own golden-update path, and read the diff to see only the script-tag change.
* **Test seams:** `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js` (reads `public/cost-format.js`; used by `lin-3833-run-control` and `flight-companion-client`) — keep the name and `loadCostFormat(sandbox)` signature but make it set `sandbox.window.CostFormat` from the real `lib/cost-format.js` import, so those two suites do not change. `tests/unit/observation-scan-due.test.js:59` lists `'cost-format.js'` in `loadWorld` scripts — switch it to `loadCostFormat`. `tests/unit/cost-read.test.js` imports only the lib file; confirm it needs nothing (the brief lists it).
* **Census:** `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js` `FORMAT_ALLOW` drop `public/cost-format.js`, and the header comment and the failure-message text that name it. Silent-staleness note: nothing fails on an extra entry, so check by eye.
* **Comments and docs that name the twin:** `lib/cost-format.js` header ("The browser twin is…"), replaced by one line saying it is also served to the browser at `/shared/cost-format.js` and so must stay a leaf; `docs/architecture/source-map.md` (its `cost-format.js` line, and the `lib/vendor-assets.js` line if there is one, gain the shared route; run `tests/unit/docs-architecture-anchor-resolver.test.js`).
* **Not places:** `tests/unit/cost-format-parity.test.js`'s server-side assertions are not restating; see step 4.

### Steps, in order

1. **Docs first.** `CLAUDE.md` "no frameworks, no build step": add the reading and limits in a sentence or two (browser may import natively; shared modules are leaf modules served by allow-list, never by directory; classic-script views and `vm` loaders stay until a module-capable client test loader exists). Add the same as a Lessons entry in `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`, with its reason (the copies came from reading the rule as "no sharing"). Keep Lessons under 6144 bytes. Check whether a CLAUDE.md census test pins its text.
2. **Serve it.** `SHARED_MODULES` + router mount in `lib/vendor-assets.js` (a `rootDir` option beside `nodeModulesDir` so a test can point it at a bad directory); `server.js` mount stays immediately before `express.static('public')`, as `vendor-assets.test.js` requires. Module scripts need a JavaScript MIME type: `sendFile` provides it for `.js`; the test asserts it.
3. **Shim and page emission.** `public/cost-format-global.js`; `page.js` module entries; change the five renderer lists; regenerate the golden.
4. **Retire.** Delete `public/cost-format.js` and `tests/unit/cost-format-parity.test.js`. The parity file also holds the only direct tests of `lib/cost-format.js`'s rules (the input table, "unknown never a dollar figure", "complete zero is $0.00", all of `sumWords`). Deleting them would loosen a guard, so move the server-side half unchanged into `tests/unit/cost-format.test.js` and drop only the comparison against the browser copy.
5. **Tests that make the new shape safe** (witnesses below), then update the census, fixture and `observation-scan-due`.
6. **Area note Waiting entries** (each starts with a `public/` or `lib/` path, no line numbers): (a) `public/common.js` — the globals it exports, and its self-declared "client twins" of `lib/task-page-href.js`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js`, `lib/ship-layout.js`, `lib/prompt-formatters.js` (the first two are leaf, same-shape next slices; the last two import other modules, so single-file serving will not do); (b) `tests/helpers/client-world`-style module-capable loader — cite `lib/components/page.js`'s classic-script emission and `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js`: needed before any view becomes a module; (c) `public/observation.js` — find out why it is \~5,000 lines; count logic and comment separately. The two surveys disagree on its comment lines (open-0: \~1,985; global: 1,006); I reproduce 1,985 of 4,679 non-blank lines counting `*`, `//` and `/*` lines, so state the counting method in the entry. Existing entries on keepalive `statusCode` readers and `buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors` are untouched.
7. **Report and stop.** PR text lists what is shared, what is retired (file and line counts), the lightening numbers with comments counted apart, and says the next slice waits for John.

### Witnesses (each fails before, passes after)

* **Shape of what is served:** a request to `/shared/cost-format.js` returns 200, a JavaScript content type, and exactly the bytes of `lib/cost-format.js`; `/shared/` anything else, and `/lib/cost-format.js`, return 404. Fails before: route absent.
* **Boot fails on a missing file:** the router built over an empty root throws, like the vendor one.
* **Purity rule (a test that tries what the guard is for):** every file in `SHARED_MODULES` has no `import` statement, no `node:` or bare-specifier reference, and no top-level `window|document|process|require`. Include a synthetic bad module that must be named, as `cost-read-census.test.js` does for its rules.
* **Ordering guarantee:** each of the four consumer scripts loads in the `vm` world with `window.CostFormat` *absent* and does not throw at load; then the global is set and the cost paths run and produce the same strings as before. Fails if a consumer ever reads the global eagerly.
* **Every page that needs the shim has it:** a test over `lib/` for each `public/*.js` file that mentions `window.CostFormat`, any `lib/` file whose scripts list names that file must also list the module shim, as `{ module: … }`. This catches a sixth page added later, and today's three the brief missed.
* **Page emission:** `renderPage` emits `<script type="module" src>` for a module entry and `<script src>` for a string; the task-page golden shows it.
* **Real browser (a** `vm` **cannot prove module order, MIME or CSP):** one Playwright check, on the cheapest existing spec whose page carries the shim (workspace KPIs or flight companion), asserting `window.CostFormat.formatUsd(0.004)` is `<$0.01`, with no console errors and no CSP violations. This also covers the hash-based CSP (`lib/security-headers.js`): `script-src 'self'` should admit a same-origin module, and the check is what confirms it.
* **The retirement itself:** `public/cost-format.js` and `cost-format-parity.test.js` absent; `FORMAT_ALLOW` has no `public/` entry; the existing census cases still fail a hand-made `$…toFixed` in a new `public/` file (the guard the parity file stood next to).
* Run the unit suites named (`lin-3833-run-control`, `flight-companion-client`, `observation-scan-due`, `cost-read`, `cost-read-census`, `vendor-assets`, `render-pages`, the docs anchor resolver) and the full unit run.

### Likeliest ways this breaks

1. **A page without the shim, or a consumer that reads the global at load.** The page works until the first cost shows, then throws in a handler. Covered by the page-has-shim test and the ordering test; the browser check confirms real timing.
2. **The module script is refused** (wrong MIME type, a CSP surprise, or the import URL not on the allow-list), so `window.CostFormat` never exists and nothing loud happens until a cost is drawn. Covered by the MIME/404 test and the real-browser check.
3. **A silent loosening:** deleting the parity file drops the server-side "never `$0.00` for an unknown" assertions. Covered by step 4's move and the retirement witness. A smaller one: the golden or `FORMAT_ALLOW` goes stale without failing.

### Session fit and review

`fits one session`. It is one shared piece, a handful of files and one real-browser check; I can name nothing one session would lose track of.

## Implementation Plan

**Plan status.** Revised after the Plan Review Verdict (Request Changes, 1 blocking finding, 8 builder notes) at HEAD `4b5001ddf`, which is still `origin/main`. Re-grounded: `git log --since=2026-11-13T12:08:10Z` over every path named below is empty. I re-read the review's blocking claim in the source: `public/workspace-kpis.js` calls `charts.draw('cost', …)` at the top of its IIFE, `public/chart-helpers.js` `draw` does `new Chart(canvas, …)` synchronously, and the y-axis `ticks.callback` is `window.CostFormat.formatUsd(Number(v))` (`public/workspace-kpis.js:138`). The finding is correct. Area notes read: `docs/areas/README.md`, `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md` (2,734 bytes in all; Lessons well under the 6,144 cap).

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The ask: browser code that shares rather than restates, no build step, taken in small slices, the reading of the rule written into the project's notes, then a pause for John. John ruled the size: just the task, one cost formatter shared, no cuts (the size record above). Done is the ticket's Done-when:

1. The reading of "no build step" (the browser may import natively, with its limits) is in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`.
2. `lib/cost-format.js` is the only implementation of `formatUsd`; the browser runs those same bytes. `public/cost-format.js` and `tests/unit/cost-format-parity.test.js` are gone and the PR names them as retired.
3. The PR says in numbers what got lighter (the 34-line browser IIFE replaced by a shim of a few lines), counts comment edits apart from logic, and says plainly that total repo lines may rise because the new guards are tests.
4. The builder then **stops**. No second slice starts before John has read the result.

Cuts to the `## As asked` block: **none**. Reworking a view "after finding out why it got so large" is not delivered here; that is John's size ruling (this slice touches no view's structure), not a cut by this plan. It goes to the area note as Waiting.

### Which way, and why

* **Serve the shared module through the existing allow-list**: in `lib/vendor-assets.js`, a second frozen map `SHARED_MODULES` (URL → repo file; first entry `/shared/cost-format.js` → `lib/cost-format.js`), validated with `statSync` at boot, with a `rootDir` option beside `nodeModulesDir` so a test can point it at an empty directory. The router factory may be shared; `VENDOR_ASSETS` stays a separate, unchanged map because `tests/unit/vendor-assets.test.js` pins exactly its three URLs. The mount stays immediately before `express.static('public')`. Set aside: a second `express.static('lib')` (publishes all server source); moving the file into `public/` (server renderers would import from the web root).
* **Bridge to classic scripts with a deferred module shim**, `public/cost-format-global.js`: imports `formatUsd` from `/shared/cost-format.js`, sets `window.CostFormat = { formatUsd }`. No view becomes a module; `common.js` and the `vm` loaders are untouched. Set aside: converting a consumer to a module (needs a module-capable client test loader, its own slice); keeping `public/cost-format.js` as a wrapper (a file whose name claims to be the formatter).
* `lib/components/page.js` learns one thing: a `scripts` entry may be `{ module: '/x.js' }`, emitted as `<script type="module" src>`; strings stay classic. Explicit beats sniffing a filename. The shim takes the place of `/cost-format.js` in each list.
* **The ordering rule, restated (this answers the blocking finding):** a module shim runs after parsing, so **no consumer may read** `window.CostFormat` **during script execution, including through a callback a library runs synchronously.** Three consumers satisfy this as they are (`public/flight-companion.js` reaches the formatter from its `DOMContentLoaded` handler; `public/observation.js` from `init` on `DOMContentLoaded`; `public/prompt-section.js` after a fetch). `public/workspace-kpis.js` does not: Chart.js's constructor lays out the scales and calls `ticks.callback` while the script first runs. **Fix at the cause:** run that file's IIFE body from a `DOMContentLoaded` listener (module scripts run before it). This changes when the page draws, not what it draws, and is not a view rework. Set aside: making the callbacks tolerate an absent formatter (would draw wrong ticks, silently), and making the shim a classic script (impossible: the import is the point).
* **Retirement is integral:** the restated formatter and its parity test go in the same PR as the sharing (the failed-consolidation pattern in `docs/papers/harbour/the-second-copy.md` §9–10).
* Shared modules are **leaves**: no imports, no Node built-ins, no DOM at load.

### Where the behaviour lives (every place, in scope)

"The browser has its own formatUsd, and pages load it as `/cost-format.js`" lives here. How I know I have them all: `grep -rIn "cost-format\|CostFormat" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git`, ignoring dated records under `docs/reviews|papers|plans`; run again after building and read every hit. Checked at HEAD, the list below is every hit.

* **Six renderers list** `/cost-format.js` (the brief named two): `lib/render.js:384`, `lib/render-flight-companion.js:400`, `lib/render-observation.js:366`, `lib/render-swipe.js:149`, `lib/render-task-page.js:82` (declared as `const SCRIPTS`, not `scripts: [...]`), `lib/render-workspace-kpis.js:226`. All six get the shim entry.
* **Consumers of** `window.CostFormat`**:** `public/flight-companion.js:428`, `public/observation.js:3992`, `public/prompt-section.js:1506`, `public/workspace-kpis.js:134,138`. Only `workspace-kpis.js` changes in behaviour (above). The other three change **comments only**: `flight-companion.js:419-426` and `observation.js:3975-3976,3989` say "restated here / no module graph to lib/" and name `public/cost-format.js`; `prompt-section.js:1505` names it. Point them at the shim and drop the misleading reasoning; count these as comment edits.
* **Golden:** `tests/fixtures/render-task-page-golden.json` embeds the script tags. Regenerate with `UPDATE_RENDER_TASK_PAGE_GOLDEN=1`; read the diff, which must be only the script-tag change.
* **Test seams:** `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js` keeps `loadCostFormat(sandbox)` (synchronous) but statically imports `formatUsd` from `lib/cost-format.js` and assigns `sandbox.window.CostFormat = { formatUsd }` (plain strings cross the vm boundary safely); drop `COST_FORMAT_SRC` (no other importer). `lin-3833-run-control` and `flight-companion-client` then need no change. `tests/unit/observation-scan-due.test.js:59` lists `'cost-format.js'` in `loadWorld` scripts: switch to `loadCostFormat`. `tests/unit/cost-read.test.js` imports only the lib file: confirm it needs nothing.
* **Census:** `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js` `FORMAT_ALLOW` (line 85), its header (lines 14-15) and the failure-message text name `public/cost-format.js`; remove them. Nothing fails on a stale extra entry, so check by eye.
* **Comments and docs naming the twin:** `lib/cost-format.js:12` ("The browser twin is…") becomes one line saying it is also served at `/shared/cost-format.js` and so must stay a leaf; `docs/architecture/source-map.md:149` and its `lib/vendor-assets.js` line gain the shared route (run `tests/unit/docs-architecture-anchor-resolver.test.js`).

### Steps, in order

1. **Docs first.** `CLAUDE.md` is at 110/110 lines and 11,950/12,000 bytes (`tests/unit/claude-md-line-budget.test.js`). Rewrite line 43, "Keep it minimal - no frameworks, no build step", in place to a short reading (the browser may import natively; shared modules are leaves served by allow-list) plus a pointer to `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md` for the limits. If it goes over 12,000 bytes, trim elsewhere in the same commit and say in the PR which text went. Put the limits and the reason in a new Lessons entry in the area note: leaf modules only; served by allow-list, never by directory; classic-script views and `vm` loaders stay until a module-capable client test loader exists; consumers never read a shared global during script execution; the copies came from reading the rule as "no sharing". 2. **Serve it.** `SHARED_MODULES`, `rootDir`, mount (see Which way). The route sends `.js` with a JavaScript MIME type; the test asserts it.
3. **Shim and page emission.** `public/cost-format-global.js`; `page.js` module entries; the six renderer lists; the golden.
4. **Fix workspace-KPI initialization.** Wrap the IIFE body of `public/workspace-kpis.js` so it runs on `DOMContentLoaded`; keep its early-return guards inside. Update its header comment to say why.
5. **Retire.** Delete `public/cost-format.js` and `tests/unit/cost-format-parity.test.js`. Move the parity file's server-side half unchanged (input table, "unknown never a dollar figure", "complete zero is $0.00", all of `sumWords`) into `tests/unit/cost-format.test.js`; drop only the comparison against the browser copy. Deleting those would loosen a guard.
6. **Tests that make the new shape safe** (witnesses below), then the fixture, census and `observation-scan-due` updates, the consumer comment edits, and the doc/comment updates above.
7. **Area note Waiting entries** (each starts with a `public/`, `lib/` or `tests/` path, no line numbers): (a) `public/common.js`: the globals it exports and its self-declared "client twins" of `lib/task-page-href.js`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js`, `lib/ship-layout.js`, `lib/prompt-formatters.js` (the first two are leaf, same-shape next slices; the last two import other modules, so single-file serving will not do); (b) `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js`: a module-capable client-test loader is needed before any view becomes a module (cite `lib/components/page.js`'s classic emission); (c) `public/observation.js`: find out why it is about 5,000 lines. State the counting method: lines starting with `*`, `//` or `/*`, which gives 1,985 comment lines among 4,679 non-blank lines (I reproduced this). Say the global survey's 1,006 used a different method; do not set the two figures side by side. Existing keepalive `statusCode` and `buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors` entries stay untouched.
8. **Report and stop.** The PR names the retirements (files and line counts), reports the 34-line IIFE against the shim, counts comment edits separately, says total lines may rise, notes any CLAUDE.md text trimmed, and says the next slice waits for John.

Unknown `/shared/*` and `/lib/cost-format.js` return a real 404 **through the full** `server.js` **app**, not just the router, so a catch-all cannot turn them into a 200 HTML page. * **Page emission:** `renderPage` emits `<script type="module" src>` for a module entry and `<script src>` for a string; the task-page golden shows it.

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "Side rail and other UI improvements are important purely because the current ones are just mostly the original ones and are due a bit of a sprinkling. But! The front end code is messy." Likely this will take a fair amount of hand holding."

On main (9 Nov), no browser file can import another, nine browser files restate logic the server already has, and the largest browser file is 5,019 lines.

* Anything bigger that a slice spots is left out of it and goes into the area's note.
* The side rail and the visual refresh come after, built on the cleaner code.
* No view is retired unless John rules it.

John expects agents to reach for big moves here: "very likely to get agents trying really hard to do big things when we want small." So the size is John's call, and for this work it's small.
